image.upscale.title: Upscale Image
image.upscale.pickCropNote: Click the thumbnail to move the preview area.
image.upscale.sizeHint: Both sides must be at least the original, up to {max}×.
image.upscale.method.ai.note: AI restores detail in blurry areas and removes JPEG artefacts and noise. It recognises the kind of picture and picks a suitable model.
image.upscale.method.hq.note: A classical, edge-preserving method. Faster than AI and keeps the original texture.
image.upscale.method.smooth.note: Smooth interpolation: few jaggies, but less sharp.
image.upscale.method.pixel.note: Enlarges pixels as they are. Best for pixel art.
image.upscale.pixelArtNote: This looks like pixel art, so "Pixel art" is chosen. AI would smear the pixels like paint.
image.upscale.aiTooLarge: This picture is too large for AI; the classical method (Sharp) is used instead.
image.upscale.canvas: Enlarge the canvas by the same factor
image.upscale.note16: 16-bit document: the layer is enlarged from the 8-bit values Omniweave edits and saved as 16-bit, so its fine 16-bit gradations are reduced to 8-bit steps.
image.upscale.note16Png: 16-bit PNG: enlarged from 8-bit values and saved as an 8-bit PNG, so its fine 16-bit gradations are reduced.
image.upscale.noteImage: The picture is saved again in its own format (JPEG, PNG, WebP) with its metadata; undo brings back the original.
image.upscale.noteRaster: The layer grows from its top-left corner. One undo step.
image.upscale.ribbonTip: Upscale Image: enlarge 2, 3 or 4 times with AI detail restoration
image.upscale.aiFallback: AI isn't available; using the classical method ({error})
image.upscale.refuse.adjust: Adjustment layers have no pixels to enlarge.
image.upscale.refuse.text: Rasterize the text layer first, then upscale it.
image.upscale.refuse.svg: SVG pictures are vectors and stay sharp at any size; just resize them.
image.upscale.refuse.cmyk: Layers of CMYK documents are not upscaled: their ink (C, M, Y, K) proportions can't be kept. Convert the document to RGB first.
image.upscale.refuse.hdr: Layers of 32-bit (HDR) documents are not upscaled: brightness above white can't be kept.
image.upscale.err.notLarger: The result must be larger than the original ({w} × {h} px). Use Image Size to make it smaller.
image.upscale.err.tooLarge: The result ({w} × {h} px) is too large: at most 30,000 px a side and {mp} MP in total.
